threads.body:
`Optional[...]` does more than make a field non-required: pydantic adds `anyOf: [..., {"type": "null"}]` to the schema, so every optional field now also accepts `null`. In JSON Schema those are two separate decisions, and the widely used schemas I checked make fields optional without allowing `null`:

| Schema | `null` allowed |
|---|---|
| [OpenAPI 3.1 meta-schema](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/3.1/schema/2022-10-07), [MCP](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/schema/2025-06-18/schema.json), [ESLint](https://json.schemastore.org/eslintrc.json) | nowhere |
| [Docker Compose](https://github.com/compose-spec/compose-spec/blob/main/schema/compose-spec.json), [GitHub Actions](https://json.schemastore.org/github-workflow.json) | only for empty YAML keys (`on: { push: }`) |
| [tsconfig](https://json.schemastore.org/tsconfig.json) | only where `null` means "reset the inherited value" |
| [CloudEvents](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/formats/cloudevents.json) | on a few optional attributes |
| [Kubernetes](https://github.com/yannh/kubernetes-json-schema) (generated) | everywhere, added by the converter |

The [Google JSON style guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/jsoncstyleguide.xml) also says to drop optional or null properties rather than emit them. Protobuf's [JSON mapping](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json/) omits unset fields and lets parsers treat `null` as unset, but it never puts `null` into a schema.

Dropping the `null` branch shouldn't hurt consumers either:
- Python code generated from the schema (e.g. [datamodel-code-generator](https://github.com/koxudaxi/datamodel-code-generator)) already turns non-required properties into `str | None = None`, with or without the `null` branch.
- Most JSON parsers treat `null` like a missing field by default or let you configure it (Go `encoding/json`, serde `Option`, Jackson `@JsonSetter(nulls=...)`, kotlinx `explicitNulls`).

What do you think about using `SkipJsonSchema[None]`? Anyone reading `models.py` still sees that `None` is expected, and the schema just says `"type": "string"`:

```suggestion
    content: Union[str, SkipJsonSchema[None]] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Text content sent to or received from the model.",
    )
```
